steps.text: Cook and stir zucchini and lemon juice in a large saucepan over medium heat until zucchini is tender, 15 to 20 minutes. Stir in 1 cup sugar, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, and nutmeg; cook for 1 more minute. Remove from the heat and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 10x15-inch baking dish.

Combine flour and 2 cups sugar in a large bowl. Cut in butter with a pastry blender or two knives until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Stir 1/2 cup of the crumb mixture into the cooked zucchini mixture.

Press 1/2 of the remaining crumb mixture into the bottom of the prepared pan. Spread zucchini mixture over top, then sprinkle with remaining crumb mixture. Sprinkle with remaining 1 teaspoon cinnamon.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is golden, 35 to 40 minutes. Serve warm or cold.

raw_recipe.headline: Zucchini Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: In this zucchini cobbler recipe, zucchini is cooked in lemon juice, spiced with cinnamon and nutmeg, baked in a crumble crust, and served hot or cold.

review.reviewBody: Great recipe. One suggestion. Remove the seeds from the Zucchini. That will take away the after taste and the slices look like apple slices. Also make sure the zucchini is sliced very thin.

Seeded zucchini. Used brown sugar, truvia, and sugar. And replaced 1 cup flour with old-fashioned oats. Baked crust 10 minutes before adding filling to keep from going soggy. Served warm with vanilla ice cream. I was "sampling" the zucchini mixture a lot before it made it to the oven. Very good if you like sugar!

I loved this recipe, i thought it was delicious. I was showered with compliments and everyone was fooled that it wasn't apple cobbler. After reading lots of reviews i decided to reduce the amount of zucchini and did four cups instead of eight and i also decided to prebake the bottom layer of the cobbler to make sure it wasn't soggy. what a great way to get your vegetables in with delicious flavoring! i will definitely be making this again.

This is a great recipe. I didn't use 8 cups of zucchini because I didn't have that much. I adjusted the lemon juice as well, I only used 1/2 a cup for 5 cups of zucchini and it was perfect. My husband who is a picky eater was fooled by this. He thought this was the best apple cobbler he had ever eaten and was shocked to learn that it was zucchini. I removed the seeds and peeled the zucchini. Doing that, I think, helps mimic and apple.

This is a great recipe. I didn't use 8 cups of zucchini because I didn't have that much. I adjusted the lemon juice as well, I only used 1/2 a cup for 5 cups of zucchini and it was perfect. My husband who is a picky eater was fooled by this. He thought this was the best apple cobbler he had ever eaten and was shocked to learn that it was zucchini. I removed the seeds and peeled the zucchini. Doing that, I think, helps mimic and apple.

The first time I made this I did not take the seeds out of the zucchini and I could taste them after they were cooked. I also thought the recipe was way too sweet and called for too much sugar. 
I just made this again with seeding the zucchini and I cut the sugar in half and it was perfect! Tastes just like apple cobbler. Yummy with some vanilla ice cream!

It’s wild that this actually works. I would never know that it wasn’t apple! It’s quite sweet so I think you could cut the sugar a little bit and have it still turn out nice or maybe add a little salt to cut it. Like another reviewer said, I thought that the crust to filling ratio was off a little bit. I made extra squash and assembled two 9 x 9 cobblers. I took inspiration from another recipe and added a tablespoon of Sriracha to the filling on one- it does not make it spicy, that adds a little more depth. I am also high altitude and ended up needing to add about an extra 15 minutes to the big time as the flour was raw up until that point. But super good, highly recommend you try this.

Worked great! I did make some pretty significant changes. I like to eliminate as much added sugar as possible, so I did the following:
- reduced zucchini and replaced with: 
- added about 2 peeled apples
- 6-8 strawberries
- 1 plum
- 1 banana
banana
- I did NOT put any sugar in the fruit mixture
- only put about 1/2 cup of sugar in crumb topping
- replaced about 1/3 of flour with oat flour and added about 1/2 cup oats. 
It came out very well. Even my husband liked it. Tasted kind of like strawberry rhubarb.

The overall flavor is good. I liked the lemon juice, which gave it an apple like taste. I sliced the zucchini thinly and only cooked for 5 minutes, which was plenty. It calls for too much flour, sugar and butter. I cut back on the flour by about a half cup, and it still was too thick for me. I would only put a few tablespoons of topping in the zucchini mixture and would leave off the bottom crust.

I really liked it, the crust is quite thick compared to the zucchini layer so I might even use 10 cups next time as they do cook down. My son has a dairy allergy so I had to make it with smart balance spread. It worked perfectly and was the right crispyness on top and chewyness on the bottom. I baked the bottom crust by its self for 10 minutes before adding the last two layers and baking the recommended time. pre baking the bottom crust kept it from getting soggy.

This cobbler is excellent. What a great way to get your veggies and also have the wonderful experience of having an apple cobbler. I made it but cut the butter to 1 cup and then left everything else the same. After adding the top flour mixture I added 1/2 cup of milk on top and mixed with the top flour and gently worked it in only the top flour so it would not be dry on top. I then added cinnamon/sugar over the top. It baked up with a very nice top crust with a sweet crunchy top and then the caramelized faux apple interior was absolutely divine. We will definitely be using this a lot in the future. I am going to also try adding flavoring to the zucchini mixture or maybe 1 box of flavored jello before baking. Thank you again for this nice find.

this was absolutely the bomb! it really does taste like apples. i cubed ours and simmered it in the lemon juice a little longer because of that, but that was the only real change. its insanely good w/ just a little vanilla ice cream on the side.
The filling could be thicker and more flavorful

Absolutely delicious as is and probably better than apple cobbler. The crumb mixture is amazing and the zucchini tastes better than apples as they get a delicious zing from the lemon juice. Thanks for a wonderful recipe! Definitely peel the zucchini and remove the seeds, also cut thin as other reviewers have said.

peel and de-seed two zucchini and cut them in really thin slices to look like apples or in small chunks. It's worth the effort because it really does taste like apples and is super sweet like cobbler. You can't tell that its not apples.
Made it same as recipe everyone thought it was Apple Cobbler
I've taken this to potlucks and fooled many people! Love it!

Excellent recipe although grated zucchini, instead of cubed, is my preferred texture. Try “Peachini Cobbler” with 50/50 cubed peach and grated zucchini - there is a good balance of the these flavours in the result.

It was super delicious ! I did use stevia & cane sugar mix & adjusted the recipe with that, as stevia is sweeter than white sugar . Had so many zucchini’s growing In the garden & decided to get creative I am grateful for this recipe !!!
